### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via backfillSummaryNulls (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via skipAutomations (symbol, a field of interface SummaryBackfillOptions))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via backfillSummaryNulls (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via syncSchemas (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL; a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 81 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bd91a12740a08bb74b3be615774fa130bbe87c2b` — the merge of head `7c933a0e63da117789434457bc73a63fde359e92` into base `951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bd91a12740a08bb74b3be615774fa130bbe87c2b && git checkout bd91a12740a08bb74b3be615774fa130bbe87c2b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f 7c933a0e63da117789434457bc73a63fde359e92 && git checkout -B drift-repro 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f && git merge --no-ff 7c933a0e63da117789434457bc73a63fde359e92

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Under area-rules 04:37Z the review thread writes this record in the same pass as the L1 read (L1 verdict: the next comment).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right.** `packages/objectql` publishes `exports` `.` and `./core`. The root `index.ts` adds `export type { SummaryMaterialiseOutcome }`, and the `ObjectQL` class gains two public methods, `materialiseAddedSummaries()` and `sealSummariesMaterialisedAtBoot()`. Both are additive, and no existing member changes signature. `IObjectQLEngine` is untouched, so no implementer of the contract is asked for anything new. `syncSchemas()` keeps its `Promise<void>` signature. Its behaviour widens: it now also writes computed values into stored rows still `NULL`, which the changeset states.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is right.** Nothing an author can write changes: no key, value or metadata type. Summary fields already exist, and only when the engine computes them on stored rows moves.
- **No narrowing arm.** No request that was served before is refused. The new walk never throws, because an incomplete walk is logged and reported, so the install door's answers are unchanged.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql: patch` is right. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`. There is no BREAKING banner and none is owed. `check-changeset-no-major` and `Check Changeset` are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **SQL pushdown (AGENTS.md).** The walk reuses `backfillSummaryNulls` as it stands: one `aggregateSummaryValue` and one parent `update` per `NULL` parent, in keyset pages of 500, bounded at 100,000 rows per object. That is per-row work where a set-based `UPDATE … FROM (SELECT … GROUP BY)` could push down. The cause is recorded: the walk has to go through the engine's own `update` so it gets the same aggregate semantics, hooks and audit as the child-write recompute, and this PR adds no new id materialisation or in-app join of its own. Noted, not a finding.
- **Write volume at the install door.** Each backfilled parent fires the parent object's update hooks and record-change automation, and the door's HTTP answer waits for the whole walk. This is a behaviour boundary, not a contract one. It is judged in the L1 read (S1 there).
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no external author is named.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` states when an install computes the roll-ups and when the operator command is still owed. `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx` (Docs Drift) still reads true at line 331 ("`syncSchemas` applies the schema").

## Review — FAIL

Head-sha: `e3a4385d9518cac80d202d97b98624232196e753`
Area: S2 / A4 · Fixes #34096 · L1, the ordinary ACCEPT read per review-checklist.md. The `TIER_DEFAULT` contract record for the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` face is 6907485457 (PASS). It finds the declaration, the level and the boundary right. This FAIL is about one behaviour point, S1, and a delta clears it.

### S1 (should-fix): the install-door walk fires every parent's record-change automation, while the same door's own writes suppress it

`backfillSummaryNulls` writes each backfilled parent through `engine.update(parent, …, { context: { isSystem: true } })`, with no `skipAutomations`. At the install door this runs automatically, on every pre-existing parent row (up to 100,000 per object). Each write runs the parent object's metadata-bound hooks and dispatches its record-change flows. For HotCRM 6.2 → 6.4, that means every `crm_contract` with invoices fires its "on update" automations at once, during the install request.

The body's parity argument ("as the child-write recompute does") does not hold for this door:

- The child-write recompute's parent write is a `sudo()`-shaped derivative of the caller's context (`engine-summary-recompute-context.test.ts:282`), so it inherits the caller's flags. During a seed load or an import with automations off, the recompute is silent too.
- The install door's own writes are marked as end-state data, not user events. `SEED_OWNER_STAMP_CTX = { isSystem: true, skipAutomations: true }` (`marketplace-install-local-seed-owner.ts:56`) follows the seed-loader rule in `engine-execution-plumbing.ts:82` ("seed loads end-state data, not user events").
- `os migrate summary-nulls` fires automation by the operator's choice, at a time the operator picks. This walk has no operator.

So the parity that matters here is the door's own convention, and the walk breaks it.

Either of these clears S1:

- **(a)** Pass `skipAutomations: true` on the install walk's write context. One way is an optional `writeContext` / `skipAutomations` on `SummaryBackfillOptions` that only `summary-install-materialise.ts` sets, so the operator command is unchanged. Pin it in the existing 34096 file: the parent write carries `skipAutomations`, and a metadata-bound parent update hook does not fire. Also check that a chained roll-up (a parent that is itself a child of another roll-up) still recomputes. The summary recompute is engine-internal, not a metadata-bound hook, so it should.
- **(b)** Keep firing, by a seat or maintainer ruling. Record the ruling in the Acceptance notes and add one changeset sentence: "each backfilled parent's update hooks and record-change automations run once, during the install".

### Read and found right

1. **Which roll-ups are new.** The boot seals at `kernel:bootstrapped`, which comes after the install-local rehydrate at `kernel:ready`. So the rehydrate's sync gets `boot-not-complete` and walks nothing. A later sync walks only `served − recorded`. A complete walk records its keys, and an incomplete one does not. The per-engine `inFlight` chain serialises two doors' syncs, and the `recorded` set is checked inside the chained run, so the same keys are never walked twice concurrently.
2. **Callers.** The only runtime callers of `syncSchemas()` are the two `MarketplaceInstallLocal` sites: the rehydrate at 1758 (before the seal) and the install / upgrade step 4b at 3224. Step 4b runs before the package's seeds, and children those seeds insert are recomputed by the child-write path. The other callers are testkits.
3. **Null versus 0.** Every added key is named in `recomputeUndefinedOnEmpty`, so `min`/`max`/`avg` are computed. `count`/`sum` read 0 on an empty set and the rest read `null`, the same as a new row.
4. **Failure handling.** `incompleteMessage` logs at `error` once, with the consequence and the exact `os migrate summary-nulls --apply --recompute-undefined-on-empty OBJECT.FIELD` line. It never throws, so the door's answer is unchanged. Only rows still `NULL` are rewritten on retry.
5. **Tests.** 7 cases, including a real `ObjectKernel` boot. The red-first run on main is 4 failed / 2 passed, and the 2 green cases are the "runs nothing" pins. Ablations A1–A6 each turn their own pin red and were restored by blob.
6. **Docs.** `cli.mdx` states both cases that still need the command. `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx` (Docs Drift) still reads true.

### Noted, not owed

- **The install answer waits for the walk.** That can be up to 100,000 parent aggregates and updates per object inside the HTTP request. The bound and the error log cap it, but a large upgrade's install call may run long. An async walk with a status the door reports is a possible follow-up, and that is the seat's call.
- **A reinstall is not re-walked.** The recorded set only grows, so a roll-up removed by uninstall and re-added by reinstall in the same process is not walked again. If the column survives the uninstall, its values can be stale from child writes made while it was gone. The Acceptance notes name this, and `os migrate summary-nulls` covers it.
- **Boundary questions ruled A.** The roll-up that arrives with a restart is #34283. The single-object publish door is not wired.

Check-runs on the head: 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed. `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` `31eb2aeda2` is clean. The own-diff patch-id is `e9c61658ee416d4b03cd24ab18a19e2f19c5493d`. After S1, a delta L1 is owed, and so is a delta of record 6907485457, if (a) changes code.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c6ff87ce6be3c8306e560911b197b13112a453e8`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-11-16T07:08Z. Delta review of this head against PASS 6907485457 at e3a4385d (by the lane's own reviewer); claim: comment 6909795221; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in a project thread for domain:server#5 (zhuangjianguo); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

The record is owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone: the nine changed paths hold no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path, so the face is the declaration face. `e3a4385d..c6ff87ce` is one commit by the PR, `c6ff87ce6` (parent `e3a4385d`), touching five files: the changeset, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, the 34096 test file, `summary-backfill.ts` and `summary-install-materialise.ts`. It holds no main merge, so there is no merge resolution to separate. The conclusions below were re-derived on the net diff `origin/main...c6ff87ce`, not carried from 6907485457.

Prior ids. Record 6907485457 grades no finding (no M, S or N id), so there is no id to continue. Its unnumbered points, each re-read on this head:

- ① widening, protocol none, no narrowing arm: hold, with one addition the delta makes (below).
- ② `patch`: holds.
- ③ SQL pushdown note: unchanged by the delta; the per-row walk is the same code.
- ③ "Write volume at the install door": half superseded. Its first sentence (each backfilled parent fires the parent's update hooks and record-change automation) is no longer true on this head. Its second (the door's answer waits for the whole walk) still is.
- ③ Author, Docs: hold; `cli.mdx` was re-read at this head.
- S1 of the L1 read 6907503603 (not an id of the record, named because the delta exists to answer it): its option (a) is what the code now does, with the three pins it asked for. Whether that L1 clears is its own seat's verdict, not this record's.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right, and the delta adds to the same arm.** `packages/objectql` publishes `.` and `./core`. Against main the root gains `export type { SummaryMaterialiseOutcome }`; `ObjectQL` gains `materialiseAddedSummaries()` and `sealSummariesMaterialisedAtBoot()`; and, new in this delta, the root-exported `SummaryBackfillOptions` gains the optional `skipAutomations?: boolean`. All four are additive. `backfillSummaryNulls` keeps its signature, and with the key omitted its write context is the bare system context it was (`summary-backfill.ts:343`), which the CONTROL case pins. `IObjectQLEngine` and `SummaryBackfillEngine` are untouched. `syncSchemas()` keeps its promise-of-void signature.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is right.** The delta introduces no key, value or metadata type an author writes. `ExecutionContext.skipAutomations` already exists in the published spec (`execution-context.zod.ts:629`); the delta adds one more in-process setter of it and changes nothing in `packages/spec`.
- **No narrowing arm.** No request served on main is refused on this head. The only two callers of `backfillSummaryNulls` are the walk and `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/summary-nulls.ts`, and the second is outside the diff and passes no new option.
- **The behaviour the delta changes is behaviour this PR itself introduced.** On main `syncSchemas()` writes no row, so "the install walk fires parent automations" never shipped; turning them off inside the PR takes nothing from a released consumer.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql: patch` is right: a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). No BREAKING banner is owed. The changeset text was rewritten in the delta and now states the automations-off write, the still-running roll-up recompute, the unchanged operator command and the new option by name; each sentence agrees with the code read.
- CI on this head: 53 check-runs, 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed, none queued or in progress. `Check Changeset` is success. `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` at `951eceeee` is clean. Nothing is pending for the seat to wait on.
CI completed before posting: 53 check-runs on this head, 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **What the flag skips, and what it does not.** The published contract for `skipAutomations` (`execution-context.zod.ts`, `hook.zod.ts:1460`) is: hooks bound from metadata and record-change flow dispatch are skipped; hooks registered in code keep running; only the system principal may take an app's declared controls off a write. The walk's write is `isSystem` and sets the flag in-process, with no request field reaching it, so it sits inside that rule. The same context shape is already the install door's own (`marketplace-install-local-seed-owner.ts:56`) and the seed-ownership claims'.
- **A stored field a parent hook derives from a roll-up is not derived by the walk.** With automations off, a metadata-bound `beforeUpdate` on the parent that computes another stored column from the new roll-up does not run on a backfilled row; it runs at that row's next ordinary write, or when the operator runs `os migrate summary-nulls`. The changeset and `cli.mdx` say no metadata-bound hook runs; neither names this consequence. The measured app is not affected: the three HotCRM figures on the card are each a direct `summary`, with no hook between them. Flag, not a finding; it is the stated price of the L1's option (a).
- **A chained roll-up moves under the same flag.** The parent write's recompute of a roll-up over that parent runs (pinned: the account is walked before the contract, reads `0`, and is moved to the sum by the contract's write). That second write inherits the context, so the grandparent's metadata-bound hooks are silent too. Consistent with the rule; noted so nobody reads "a backfilled parent" as the only silent object.
- **The door's answer still waits for the walk.** Up to 100,000 aggregates and updates per object inside the install request. Unchanged by the delta, and the prior record's note stands.
- **SQL pushdown.** Unchanged: per-row aggregate and update through the engine's own verb, no new id materialisation or in-app join in the delta.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` at the `os migrate summary-nulls` section agrees with the code on all four statements it makes about the walk (automations off, chained roll-up recomputed, the command run by hand keeps them on, `min`/`max`/`avg` included).
- **Author.** `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no external author.

### ④ Design judgment

The declaration face carries no ④ of its own; this is the delta's one design choice, read against the code it cites.

- The option is opt-in on the shared function and set at one site (`summary-install-materialise.ts:162`), so the operator command cannot drift into the door's behaviour by default. The value is compared with `=== true`, and the read contexts (`find`, `aggregate`) stay on the bare system context, so only the parent `update` changes.
- The three new cases each pin a distinct claim: the flag on every parent write plus a bound hook that stays silent; the chained roll-up, in the order that makes the pin non-vacuous; and the control that the operator path still fires. The file is now 10 cases.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit) — the PR body still describes the previous head: "7 cases" and "expected 7/7" where the file holds 10, and "The write is the child-write recompute's ... with `{ isSystem: true }`" with no mention of `skipAutomations`. If the body becomes the squash message, bring it in line with the changeset. Continues no prior id.
- N2 (nit) — one sentence in `cli.mdx` could name the consequence in the second ③ flag: a column a parent hook derives from a new roll-up is filled at that row's next write or by the command. Continues no prior id.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `c6ff87ce6be3c8306e560911b197b13112a453e8`
Area: S2 / A4 · Fixes #34096 · delta L1 against my FAIL 6907503603 at `e3a4385d`. The PR's one new commit is `c6ff87ce6b`. The `TIER_DEFAULT` record at this head is review#2's delta PASS 6909874303. It is the newest record naming this head and it governs, so I am not posting a second one.

1. **S1 is cleared by option (a).**
   - `SummaryBackfillOptions` gains an opt-in `skipAutomations`. Unset, the write context is the bare `{ isSystem: true }` it always was. Set, it is `{ isSystem: true, skipAutomations: true }`.
   - Only `walkAdded` (`summary-install-materialise.ts`) sets it. That matches the install door's own `SEED_OWNER_STAMP_CTX` and the seed-loader rule (end-state data, not user events).
   - `os migrate summary-nulls` passes no flag, so the operator path keeps firing at the time the operator picks.
2. **The three pins cover what I asked for.**
   - The install walk's parent writes all carry `skipAutomations: true`, and a metadata-bound `beforeUpdate` on the parent does not fire (`boundCalls` stays empty), while the value lands (40000).
   - A chained roll-up still moves: the account over the contracts the walk just filled reads 40000. The engine's recompute is not a metadata-bound automation.
   - The CONTROL shows the operator backfill writes with `skipAutomations` undefined, and the bound hook fires.
   - The body records red-first and the A7 ablation.
